This matches the fence exactly (ext/grip/*, ext/drawer/rail.js, ext/drawer/rail.css, plus the task's own log file). Everything is committed, tested, and documented. Time to report back to the parent.

## Done — `ext/grip` now works on both axes, and the mobile sheet has a real drag handle

**What changed** (branch `worktree/grip-everywhere`, 2 commits, `d064be81` + `5bc4239f`):

1. **`ext/grip/grip.js`** got `axis: "x"|"y"` (default `"x"`). Every existing caller (drawer, dev bar, Sidebar, `/layouts/shell/`, ai2, files, columns) is untouched — traced line by line, the `x` path is byte-identical. `axis: "y"` reuses the exact `from`/`mirror` pointer math already proven for `x`, just read against top/bottom instead of left/right.
2. **`ext/grip/grip.css`** — new `.grip-y` rules (mirrored geometry, `--grip-x` for the pill's cross-axis instead of `--grip-y`), a shared `@media (pointer: coarse), (hover: none)` block that thickens the strip and makes it visible at rest on touch (both axes), and an exemption so the existing 34em hide-rule doesn't also hide the new handle.
3. **`ext/drawer/rail.js` + `rail.css`** — the ✦ sheet now has a real handle at its own top edge: starts at 50% of the viewport or the sheet's own content height if that's smaller (measured, not assumed), remembers a dragged height per device in `localStorage` (own key, try/catch both ways), and reads it back on the next open.
4. **Docs** — `ext/grip/readme.md` and `doc/decisions.md` updated truthfully with the new option and the reasoning/measurements behind each decision.

**Proof** — headless Playwright against the worktree's own server, screenshots at `public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/grip-everywhere/build/shots/` (not committed — `shots/` is gitignored by design, browsable on the dev server): 1920×1080 mouse shows the drawer's unchanged slim x-grip; a narrow desktop window (mouse, no touch) proves the y-handle stays slim/hover-only by *pointer type*, not screen width; 400×800 touch emulation shows the thicker always-visible handle, a real dispatched pointer-event drag growing the sheet from 188px to 337px, and that same 337px reading back after a reload with zero further drag.

My own smoke check (`/`, `/framework/ext/grip/`, `/framework/ext/drawer/`) is clean — zero console/page/request errors. Left for you: `ext/grip/page.js` has no live `axis:"y"` demo (the brief's own fence left it out of the touchable file list, so I read that as deliberate). Per your instructions I did not merge or touch the dev server — over to you for docs-check, review, and merge.

Status: done on my end. `axis:"x"|"y"` is built in `ext/grip`, wired into the ✦ sheet's own handle in `ext/drawer`, documented, and proven with headless screenshots — all committed on `worktree/grip-everywhere` (`d064be81`, `5bc4239f`). I reported the summary back to the parent task-mastermind (`grip-everywhere`) and am not doing further work — docs-check, fresh review, and merge are its job per my launch instructions, not mine. Nothing blocking; I'm just idle waiting to be resumed if a review finding comes back.

Done. Findings written to `public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/grip-everywhere/docs-check.md`.

Summary: the `axis` option is clear enough to use correctly from `ext/grip`'s docs alone (readme states the one-line semantics, `decisions.md` confirms `from`/`mirror` carry over unchanged and the 34em hide rule has a `.grip-y` exemption). The one real gap: `ext/drawer`'s own readme/decisions.md never mention that the ✦ mobile sheet is drag-resizable via `grip(axis:"y")` — that fact only lives in grip's doc tree, not drawer's, so a reader starting from drawer's docs would miss it entirely.

Report sent to the task mastermind. Its state shows `working`, so the message is queued/delivered — it'll pick it up and handle the merge from here.

**Summary:** All three review findings are fixed, verified, and committed (`761f1311`) on `worktree/grip-everywhere`: the dropped `html.grip-sizing` easing/cursor/select-block regression is restored (now axis-aware), the sheet's saved-height read-back is clamped the same as a live drag, and the decisions.md measurement note now states its 16px root-font-size assumption. Answers are logged on the parent task's `task.jsonl` and mirrored via `review.mjs --turns`. Reported done to `task-mastermind-grip-everywhere`, which owns the merge from here.
